title: Bill 23 financial impacts and councillor benefits
subtitle: Strategic plan approach, 2023 temporary borrowing, and a church's request for development charge relief.
overview: The committee recommended that the Region ask the province to reconsider Bill 23, extend consultation, and fund growth infrastructure so existing taxpayers do not absorb the cost {{vote:m3}}. Staff said the bill cuts development charges, which pay for growth-related roads, water, transit and housing, so costs could shift to property taxes and user rates.

On councillor benefits, the committee recommended rescinding the November 8 decision to extend post-service benefits, ending extended benefits for past councillors on December 31, 2022, and creating a citizen advisory committee on remuneration in the third year of this term {{vote:m5}}. An amendment barred that committee from considering lifetime benefits fully paid by the Region {{vote:m6}}.

The committee also recommended the approach for the 2023-2027 strategic plan and temporary borrowing by-laws for 2023. After hearing from a Waterloo church seeking relief from development charges on a new church and community centre, it directed staff to report during the 2023 budget process on other funding options. These recommendations go to Council for adoption.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended asking the province to reconsider Bill 23, extend consultation, explain its effect on housing affordability, and provide sustained infrastructure funding, with the resolution sent to provincial and municipal bodies {{vote:m3}}.

The committee recommended rescinding the November 8 decision on post-service benefits, ending extended benefits for past councillors on December 31, 2022, and preparing terms of reference for a citizen advisory committee on council remuneration and benefits {{vote:m5}}.
The committee recommended that the advisory committee's terms of reference bar it from considering post-service lifetime benefits fully paid by the Region {{vote:m6}}.
The committee recommended approving the approach, timeline and supporting principles for developing the new Corporate Strategic Plan {{vote:m4}}.
The committee recommended authorizing the Chief Financial Officer, by by-law, to borrow funds temporarily in 2023 to meet operating and capital expenditure needs.

debate: Staff argued that cutting development charges will not speed up home building and could slow it, because infrastructure may be delayed or shifted to property taxes, user rates and debt. They said the impacts are hard to quantify because provisions take effect at different times.

Councillors asked what the province means by keeping municipalities whole and whether reserve fund balances are misunderstood. Staff said tracking and reporting mechanisms are needed and that the reserves are small compared with outstanding growth-related debt.

One councillor said Bill 23 reaches beyond finances, including environmental effects, parkland and climate adaptation, and that these should not be lost in a focus on money. Another said the province treats municipalities as junior partners and called for stronger funding.

On the benefits amendment, supporters said lifetime benefits fully paid by the Region should be off the table. Opponents said it would tie the hands of the citizen committee and staff, and that scope belongs in the terms of reference.

The church delegate said the new community centre would host not-for-profit partners and free gym space, and asked for help with development charges. Councillors asked why this is a regional matter, and one asked staff to report on how many other worship centres might make similar requests.
